races.title: State Assembly, District 79
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: LaShae Sharp-Collins
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 79 since December 2024. Holds an Ed.D. from San Diego State University, where she was an adjunct professor. Worked for the San Diego County Office of Education and as district director for Shirley Weber. Assistant Majority Leader for Policy and Research.

controversies.text: In October 2022, a student in her San Diego State Africana Studies class posted on Instagram an assignment asking students to create a "slave persona", and others objected. The department chair said students were never required to dress as slaves or speak in "broken English", as some outlets reported. No official finding was reported.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed on Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association and Equality California.
In 2024 she was endorsed by the San Diego County Democratic Party. In her own survey she also listed Shirley Weber, Toni Atkins, Planned Parenthood and Sierra Club California.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from her on data centers or large-scale development. We found no record of her actions on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B and immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, gun laws, or school vouchers and teacher pay. The list of bills she sponsored did not load on the page we read, so we could not tie specific bills to these topics. Her campaign site describes passed bills only in general terms, with no bill numbers. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Her 2024 survey answers are the main source for her stated positions. She has not publicly addressed the 2022 course assignment in the sources we have.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says she was born in San Diego, and Wikipedia says she was born and raised there and graduated from Lincoln High School; her campaign site calls her a lifelong San Diegan.

cands.name: Andrew Lawson
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 79 (San Diego County) in 2026. He advanced from the June 2026 primary and lost the November general election to incumbent LaShae Sharp-Collins. The pages collected give no career or office history.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Republican Party of California and Reform California, plus several voter-guide groups, including Conservative California and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Andrew Lawson was born or raised, when he came to California, or his career and any past elected office. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found nothing on his positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or teacher pay. We found no actions he has taken in office, and no news coverage or controversies about him.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he supports empowering parents with school choice and directing funding to classrooms instead of administrative overhead. His site does not mention teacher pay.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he supports fully funding law enforcement and reversing soft-on-crime policies that have emboldened repeat offenders.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he wants to cut bureaucratic red tape that delays new construction, streamline permitting and incentivize builders to create housing. This runs against slowing growth or tightening development oversight.
